exposure: Mode of delivery: Cesarean section, vacuum extraction, spontaneous delivery
Women with obstetric anal sphincter injuries
Duration of prolonged second stage of labor
cohort: 1302 primiparous women with a second stage of labor ≥ 3 hours
finding: Vacuum extraction was associated with an increased risk of anal incontinence compared to cesarean section, while spontaneous delivery was not.
mod_finding: Compared with cesarean section, vacuum extraction was associated with anal incontinence (aOR 2.25, 95% CI 1.21-4.18) while spontaneous delivery was not (aOR 1.55, 95% CI 0.85-2.84).
